Theme

Body, health & movement

abortion noun

also have an abortion, induce an abortion, abortive

classical

Ter. Hec. 3.3.38 (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 14.20.2 (Lewis & Short)
Plin. NH 14.118: abortum facere, to cause an abortion (Lewis & Short)

abortus, abortūs m.

noun, fourth declension

abortion; miscarriage

Covers both: a miscarriage (abortum facere, to miscarry, Plin. Ep. 8.10.1) and an abortion caused by drugs or force (abortum facere with a drug as subject, Pliny). Which is meant comes from the context.

Other words

  • abortiō, abortiōnis f. — abortion, premature delivery

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Clu. 12 (Lewis & Short’s chapter); Plaut. Truc. 1.2.98 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. abortion

    In Cicero of an abortion paid for; in the Digest the drug that causes one is abortiōnis pōculum (M-O).

  • partum abigere — to procure an abortion

    also used · classical · Cic. Clu. 31: partum sibi ipsa medicāmentīs abēgisset (M-O); Tac. Ann. 14.63 (M-O)

    The phrase for the act: to drive out the unborn child. An abortifacient drug is abortīvum, abortīvī n. (Juv. 2.32, M-O).

See also pregnant, baby.

SourcesLewis & Short: abortus · Lewis & Short: abortio · Lewis & Short: abigo · Lewis & Short: abortivus
